result.title: Fine-Grained RLAIF for Visual Safety: Learning to Zoom into Hazards for Multimodal Safety Alignment
result.summary: Recent multimodal safety alignment heavily relies on a text-centric paradigm, assuming risks are explicit in language or globally prominent in images. However, real-world hazards are often visually subtle or peripheral, causing existing models to fail due to their reliance on coarse, global visual representations. In this work, we study fine-grained visual safety alignment and introduce a challenging 1,200-sample benchmark across four domains, where hazards necessitate localized inspection. To address this, we propose Fine-Grained RLAIF (FGR), a reinforcement learning framework that casts image zoom-in as a learnable perception policy. FGR employs a decomposed reward design to jointly align three core safety behaviors: (i) where to look via a visual evidence reward, (ii) when to act via a tool-formatting constraint, and (iii) how to reason via visually grounded safety explanations. FGR achieves accuracy ranging from 86.71% to 93.00%, consistently outperforming strong multimodal and agent-based baselines.

AI.brief_summary: 针对视觉风险细微、位于图像边缘导致多模态安全对齐失效的问题，构建1200样本细粒度安全基准，并提出FGR强化学习框架，把图像放大作为可学习的感知策略，用分解奖励分别约束「看哪里」「何时调用工具」和「如何给出有视觉依据的解释」。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「定位视觉证据—决定是否触发放大—再作答」的奖励分解，与关注的 LOOK/STOP 收益成本、视觉证据筛选及动态计算问题直接相关，可供核查该感知策略是否真被答案使用、以及局部放大带来的成本与泛化表现。
